In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Ha-Mim 'Ayn-Sin-Qaf. I heard Abu Ishaq say: I heard Abu 'Uthman ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqri al-Za'farani say: I heard my shaykh say: I heard Abu Bakr al-Mu'min say: I asked al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl: Why is Ha-Mim 'Ayn-Sin-Qaf separated (into its letters), while Kaf-Ha-Ya-'Ayn-Sad, and Alif-Lam-Mim-Sad are not?

He lowered his head, then turned away from him; then he repeated his question, and he gave him no answer; he repeated it a third time, and he gave him nothing. Then Hudhayfah said to him: "I will tell you about it. I know why he disliked it. It was revealed concerning a man from his household, called 'Abd al-Ilah or 'Abd Allah, who will settle on a river of the rivers of the East, and build on it two cities, and the river will be split between them. When Allah, the Exalted, permits the end of their rule and the cutting-off of their dynasty and their term, Allah will send a fire upon one of them at night, and in the morning it will be black and dark, having burned entirely, so that it is no longer in its place; and its companion will wake up amazed at how it escaped. Nothing will remain but the brightness of that day, until every stubborn tyrant of them is gathered in it, then Allah will cause it to sink with them all. Ha-Mim is justice from Him; the Sin is that which will be a trial (sayakunu fitnatan); the Qaf is that which will befall them both, these two cities."

A parallel to this interpretation is what

We were informed by 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who was told by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, who was told by 'Abd Allah ibn Makhlad, who was told by Ishaq ibn Bishr al-Kahili, who was told by 'Ammar ibn Sayf al-Dabbi Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said:

I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A city will be built between the Tigris, Dujayl, Qutrabbul and al-Sarat, in which the tyrants of the earth will gather; wealth will be brought to it, and it will be swallowed up with them." He said once: "It will be swallowed up with its people; and it will vanish more swiftly from the earth than an iron stake in soft ground."

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite (Ha-Mim Sin-Qaf) without the 'Ayn. It is said: the Sin in it refers to every division that will occur, and the Qaf refers to every community that will occur; and he would say: 'Ali used to know the trials through these two.

Likewise it is so in the codex of 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud): (Ha-Mim Sin-Qaf).

'Ikrimah said: Nafi' ibn al-Azraq asked Ibn 'Abbas about the saying of Allah: Ha-Mim 'Ayn-Sin-Qaf.

He said: "Ha" is His forbearance (halmuhu), "Mim" is His glory (majduhu), "'Ayn" is His knowledge ('ilmuhu), "Sin" is His radiance (sana'uhu), "Qaf" is His power (qudratuhu); Allah swears by them.

In the narration of Abu al-Jawza', Ibn 'Abbas said to Nafi': "'Ayn" contains punishment, "Sin" contains transformation (maskh), "Qaf" contains hurling (qadhf). This is supported by what is related in a marfu' hadith: when this verse was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) showed sorrow in his face. It was said to him: "What is this sorrow, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "I have been informed of a calamity that will descend upon my ummah: of swallowing up (khasf), transformation (maskh), and hurling (qadhf); and a fire that will gather them, and a wind that will cast them into the sea; and successive signs connected to the descent of 'Isa (peace be upon him) and the emergence of the Dajjal."

Shahr ibn Hawshab and 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: "Ha" is a war (harb) in which the humble will be exalted and the mighty humbled, among Quraysh; then it will reach the Arabs, then it will reach the non-Arabs, then it will extend until the emergence of the Dajjal.

'Ata' said: "Ha" is a war among the people of Makkah that will afflict them so severely that they eat carrion and the bones of the dead; "Mim" is a kingdom passing from one people to another; "'Ayn" is an enemy of Quraysh who will target them; "Sin" is an evil that will occur among them; "Qaf" is the all-pervading power of Allah over His creation.

Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani said: "Ha" is a war that will occur between Quraysh and the mawali (non-Arab clients), in which victory will be for Quraysh over the mawali; "Mim" is the kingdom of the Banu Umayyah; "'Ayn" is the ascendancy of the descendants of al-'Abbas; "Sin" is the splendour of al-Mahdi; "Qaf" is the strength of 'Isa (peace be upon him) when he descends, and he will kill the Christians and destroy the churches. [[al-'Umdah by Ibn Bitriq: 429, no. 898; and al-Ta'ra'if by Ibn Tawus: 176, no. 276, from al-Tha'labi.]]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Allah swore by His forbearance, His glory, His exaltedness, His splendour and His power, that He will not punish whoever returns to Him, saying "There is no god but Allah," sincerely from his heart.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Ha" is from al-Rahman; "Mim" is from al-Majid; "'Ayn" is from al-'Alim; "Sin" is from al-Quddus; "Qaf" is from al-Qahir.

Al-Suddi said: it is from the abbreviated letters of spelling (al-hija' al-muqatta'): "'Ayn" is from al-'Aziz, "Sin" is from al-Salam, "Qaf" is from al-Qadir.

It has also been said: this concerns Muhammad (ﷺ): "Ha" is his Basin (hawdhuhu al-mawrud), "Mim" is his sovereignty (mulkatuhu al-mamdud), "'Ayn" is his honour that is present ('izzuhu al-mawjud), "Sin" is his radiance that is witnessed (sana'uhu al-mashhud), "Qaf" is his standing in the praiseworthy station (maqam al-mahmud), and his nearness in honour to the Worshipped (al-Ma'bud).

"To whom He has what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and He is the Most High, the Supreme." "The heavens are almost rent apart from above them" — i.e., from the greatness and majesty of Allah above them.

Indeed, Allah is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful."

The wise said: He magnified at the beginning, then gave glad tidings and showed gentleness at the end.

"As for those who take protectors besides Him, Allah is Watcher over them" — He guards their deeds and counts their actions so as to recompense them for them. "And you are not a guardian over them" — you are only obliged to deliver the message. "And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an, that you may warn the Mother of Towns" — Makkah, meaning its people, "and those around it, and warn of the Day of Gathering, about which there is no doubt." "A party in the Garden" — by grace, and they are the believers; "and a party in the Blaze" — by justice, and they are the disbelievers.

He said: "Do you know what these two books are?" We said: "No, O Messenger of Allah."

He said to the one in his right hand: "This is a book from the Lord of the worlds, with the names of the people of Paradise, the names of their fathers and their tribes, and their number, before they settled as drops in the loins, and before they settled as drops in the wombs, while they were in the clay, laid down. 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr said: "Then why do we work?" He said: "Act, be upright and moderate, for the people of Paradise will be sealed with the deeds of the people of Paradise, however they may act; and the people of the Fire will be sealed with the deeds of the people of the Fire, however they may act." He said: "I have been informed of a calamity that will descend upon my ummah: of swallowing up (khasf), transformation (maskh), and hurling (qadhf); and a fire that will gather them, and a wind that will cast them into the sea; and successive signs connected to the descent of 'Isa (peace be upon him) and the emergence of the Dajjal."

Shahr ibn Hawshab and 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: "Ha" is a war (harb) in which the humble will be exalted and the mighty humbled, among Quraysh; then it will reach the Arabs, then it will reach the non-Arabs, then it will extend until the emergence of the Dajjal.

'Ata' said: "Ha" is a war among the people of Makkah that will afflict them so severely that they eat carrion and the bones of the dead; "Mim" is a kingdom passing from one people to another; "'Ayn" is an enemy of Quraysh who will target them; "Sin" is an evil that will occur among them; "Qaf" is the all-pervading power of Allah over His creation.

Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani said: "Ha" is a war that will occur between Quraysh and the mawali (non-Arab clients), in which victory will be for Quraysh over the mawali; "Mim" is the kingdom of the Banu Umayyah; "'Ayn" is the ascendancy of the descendants of al-'Abbas; "Sin" is the splendour of al-Mahdi; "Qaf" is the strength of 'Isa (peace be upon him) when he descends, and he will kill the Christians and destroy the churches. [[al-'Umdah by Ibn Bitriq: 429, no. 898; and al-Ta'ra'if by Ibn Tawus: 176, no. 276, from al-Tha'labi.]]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: Allah swore by His forbearance, His glory, His exaltedness, His splendour and His power, that He will not punish whoever returns to Him, saying "There is no god but Allah," sincerely from his heart.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Ha" is from al-Rahman; "Mim" is from al-Majid; "'Ayn" is from al-'Alim; "Sin" is from al-Quddus; "Qaf" is from al-Qahir.

Al-Suddi said: it is from the abbreviated letters of spelling (al-hija' al-muqatta'): "'Ayn" is from al-'Aziz, "Sin" is from al-Salam, "Qaf" is from al-Qadir.

It has also been said: this concerns Muhammad (ﷺ): "Ha" is his Basin (hawdhuhu al-mawrud), "Mim" is his sovereignty (mulkatuhu al-mamdud), "'Ayn" is his honour that is present ('izzuhu al-mawjud), "Sin" is his radiance that is witnessed (sana'uhu al-mashhud), "Qaf" is his standing in the praiseworthy station (maqam al-mahmud), and his nearness in honour to the Worshipped (al-Ma'bud).

Ibn 'Abbas said: There is no prophet who had a Book except that Ha-Mim 'Ayn-Sin-Qaf was revealed to him; therefore He said: "Thus does He reveal to you, and to those before you, Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise." Ibn Kathir recited it with a fathah on the Ha, and similarly Ibn 'Abbas related it from Ibn 'Amr, and the noun is in the nominative by way of explanation, as if he said: "He reveals to you." It was asked: "Who reveals?" He said: "Allah." This is like the reading of those who read "yusabbahu lahu fiha" (Q. 24:36) with a fathah on the ba', while the rest read it with a kasrah.

"To whom He has what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and He is the Most High, the Supreme." "The heavens are almost rent apart from above them" — i.e., from the greatness and majesty of Allah above them.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "The heavens are almost rent apart" — each one of them is almost torn asunder above the one that is next to it, from the saying of the polytheists: "Allah has taken a son" (Q. 2:116). Its counterpart is His saying: "The heavens almost burst from it, the earth splits open, and the mountains fall down in ruins, because they attribute a son to the Most Merciful" (Q. 19:90–91). "And the angels glorify the praise of their Lord and ask forgiveness for those on earth" — from the believers, as an explanation. "Ask forgiveness for those who believe. Indeed, Allah is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful."

The wise said: He magnified at the beginning, then gave glad tidings and showed gentleness at the end.

"As for those who take protectors besides Him, Allah is Watcher over them" — He guards their deeds and counts their actions so as to recompense them for them. "And you are not a guardian over them" — you are only obliged to deliver the message. "And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an, that you may warn the Mother of Towns" — Makkah, meaning its people, "and those around it, and warn of the Day of Gathering, about which there is no doubt." "A party in the Garden" — by grace, and they are the believers; "and a party in the Blaze" — by justice, and they are the disbelievers.

We were informed by the Imam Abu Mansur al-Jamshadhi, who was told by Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm, who was told by Abu 'Uthman Sa'id ibn 'Uthman ibn Habib al-Suhayy, who was told by Bishr ibn Mutar, who was told by Sa'id ibn 'Uthman, from Abu Rahawayh Judayr ibn Kurayb, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, and the Prophet (ﷺ) used to prefer 'Abd Allah over his father.

We were informed by al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh, who was told by Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i, who was told by 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, who was told by my father, who was told by Hisham ibn al-Qasim, who was told by Layth, who was told by Abu Qabil Hayy ibn Hani al-Ma'afiri, from Shafi al-Asbahi, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us one day, holding his two palms closed, and with him were two books. He said: "Do you know what these two books are?" We said: "No, O Messenger of Allah."

He said to the one in his right hand: "This is a book from the Lord of the worlds, with the names of the people of Paradise, the names of their fathers and their tribes, and their number, before they settled as drops in the loins, and before they settled as drops in the wombs, while they were in the clay, laid down. Nothing will be added to them nor subtracted from them: a complete reckoning from Allah concerning them until the Day of Resurrection." Then he said to the one in his left hand: "This is a book from the Lord of the worlds, with the names of the people of the Fire and the names of their fathers, their tribes and their number, before they settled as drops in the loins and before they settled in the wombs, while they were in the clay, laid down. Nothing will be added to them nor subtracted from them: a complete reckoning from Allah concerning them until the Day of Resurrection."

'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr said: "Then why do we work?" He said: "Act, be upright and moderate, for the people of Paradise will be sealed with the deeds of the people of Paradise, however they may act; and the people of the Fire will be sealed with the deeds of the people of the Fire, however they may act." [169] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 3/304.]]

Then he said: "A party in the Garden and a party in the Blaze" — a justice from Allah, the Exalted.

The commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 42, verses 8–22:

﴿If God had willed, He would have made them one community upon one religion.﴾ But ﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy; and the wrongdoers, the disbelievers, have no protector or helper.﴾ Or have they taken protectors besides Him? ﴿God is the Protector, and none other.﴾ ﴿He gives life to the dead﴾, meaning, by way of metaphor (majaz): because He gives life to the dead. ﴿He has power over all things﴾, in religion.

﴿Whatever you differ about, its judgment rests with God.﴾ ﴿That is God, my Lord. In Him I have put my trust, and to Him I turn back.﴾ ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth. He made for you mates from among yourselves﴾, meaning spouses (halā'il). He said "from among yourselves" because He created Eve from a rib of Adam. ﴿And of the cattle, mates; He multiplies you thereby﴾, meaning He creates you and sustains you, ﴿therein﴾, that is, in the womb. It was also said: in the belly; it was also said: in the soul; and it was said: in this manner of creation.

Mujahid said: offspring after offspring, and "of the cattle." It was also said that "fi" here means "bi" (with), i.e., He multiplies you by means of it. Ibn Kaysan said: He increases you in number.

﴿There is nothing like Him.﴾ The word "mithl" (like) is here superfluous (silah), and its meaning is: ﴿there is nothing like Him﴾ as "laysa kahuwa shay'" (there is nothing as He is). The word "mithl" was introduced for the emphasis of the statement, as in His saying: ﴿So if they believe in the like of what you believe, they are guided﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 137]. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "fa-in āmanū bi-mā āmantum bihi" (if they believe in what you believe). And Aws ibn Hajar said:

"And slain men like the trunks of palm trees, / over whom falls a pouring rain."

That is, "like trunks." And [another] — so it appears — Sa'd ibn Zayd said:

"When I see their excellence, / there is none among the people like them."

And another said:

"There is none like al-Fata Zuhayr, / a character that equals him in virtues."

It was also said that the "ka" (like) is superfluous (silah), and its meaning is: "laysa mithlahu" (there is nothing like him), as the rajaz poet said:

"And hearths like the stones [of the cooking pot]..."

So he added a second "ka" to the "ka" for the emphasis of the comparison. Another said:

"[The swift ones] drive away the shining horses on the road, / a slender [mare] like an egg in a nest."

Here he combined "ka" with "'an".

﴿And He is the Hearing, the Seeing.﴾ ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. He extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it.﴾ ﴿Indeed, He is Knower of all things.﴾ ﴿He has prescribed for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah﴾, and he is the first of the prophets of the Law (shari'ah).

﴿And what We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus﴾: they differed concerning the sense of this verse. Qatadah said: the permitting of the lawful and the forbidding of the unlawful. al-Hakam said: the forbidding of sisters, mothers and daughters. Mujahid said: God did not send any prophet without enjoining upon him the establishment of prayer, the giving of zakat, and acknowledgment of obedience to God.

﴿That is His religion which He prescribed for them﴾. This is the narration of al-Wali from Ibn 'Abbas. It was also said: the religion is monotheism (tawhid). It was also said: it is His saying ﴿that you establish the religion and do not divide over it﴾. All the prophets were sent to establish the religion, unity, community, and to abandon division and opposition. ﴿Hard upon the polytheists is what you call them to﴾, of monotheism and the rejection of idols. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿God chooses for Himself whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns back﴾, that is, He singles him out for His religion.

﴿And they did not divide﴾, meaning the people of the differing religions. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means the People of the Book. Its proof and parallel is in surah al-Bayyinah: ﴿except after clear evidence had come to them﴾ [Surah al-Bayyinah: 4].

﴿except after knowledge had come to them﴾, that is, before the sending of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his description. ﴿Out of envy among themselves.﴾ ﴿Had not a word preceded from your Lord﴾, the delay of punishment, ﴿until an appointed term﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾ by punishment.

﴿And indeed, those who were given the Book after them﴾, meaning after the earlier nations. Mujahid said: its meaning is "before them", that is, before the polytheists of Makkah, namely the Jews and the Christians. ﴿Are in disquieting doubt about it﴾. ﴿So for that, call﴾, as in His saying: ﴿because your Lord has inspired her﴾ [Surah al-Zalzalah: 5], that is, to it; i.e., to that to which those given the Book were called. ﴿And be steadfast as you were commanded﴾, that is, persist in the religion with which you were commanded. ﴿And do not follow their desires. And say: I believe in what God has sent down of Book, and I was commanded to do justice among you﴾, that is, that I should be just, or in order that I may be just, as in His saying: ﴿and we were commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 71].

Ibn 'Abbas said: that I may make you equal in religion, and that I believe in every Book and every Messenger. Others said: ﴿to do justice among you﴾ in all circumstances and affairs.

Qatadah said: The Prophet of God (ﷺ) was commanded to be just, and he was just until he died, and justice is the balance of God on earth.

It has been related to us that Dawud (peace be upon him) said: Three qualities, whoever has them is the winner: moderation in wealth and poverty, justice in contentment and anger, and goodness in secret and in public. Three qualities, whoever has them is humiliated: a greed that is obeyed, a desire that is followed, and a man's self-admiration. And four, whoever is given them has been given the good of this world and the Hereafter: a remembering tongue, a grateful heart, a patient body, and a believing wife.

﴿God is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds. There is no argument﴾, that is, no dispute, ﴿between us and you.﴾ It was abrogated by the verse of fighting. ﴿God will gather us together﴾ for the final judgment between us. ﴿And to Him is the final return.﴾ ﴿And those who argue concerning God﴾, that is, dispute about the religion of God and His Prophet, ﴿after He has been responded to﴾, that is, after people responded to him, so they became Muslims and entered his religion, because of the manifestation of his miracle and the establishment of his proof, ﴿their argument is baseless﴾, false and vanishing.

﴿With their Lord, and upon them is anger, and for them is a severe punishment.﴾ Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning the Jews and the Christians. They said: our Book is before your Book, our Prophet is before your Prophet, and we are better than you and more deserving of the truth.

﴿God is He who sent down the Book in truth, and the balance﴾, that is, justice, according to Ibn 'Abbas and most of the exegetes. Mujahid said: it is that by which weighing is done; and the meaning of the sending down of the balance is God's inspiring creatures to act by it, and His commanding justice and fairness, as in His saying: ﴿We have sent down to you clothing﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 26].

Alqamah said: the balance is Muhammad (ﷺ), who judges between them by the Book.

﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾ It did not say "qarībah" (near, feminine) because its feminine gender is not real (ḥaqīqī). Its metaphorical meaning is "the time." al-Kisa'i said: its coming is near.

﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it﴾, supposing that it will not come. ﴿And those who believe are apprehensive of it﴾, fearful of it. ﴿And they know that it is the truth. Unquestionably, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in far error.﴾

﴿God is Subtle with His servants﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: Gracious to them. 'Ikrimah: Kind to them. al-Suddi: Tender. Muqatil: Subtle toward the righteous and the wicked among them, in that He does not kill them with hunger because of their sins. al-Qurazi: Subtle with them in the presentation and the reckoning.

al-Khawafi said: Tomorrow, with the Master of creation, there is a standing for creation in which the Majestic One will question them, and the Truthful One is gentle with them concerning provision in two respects: first, that He made your provision from the good things; and second, that He did not give it to you all at once. It was also said: contentment in multiplication. al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl: in the Qur'an and its facilitation.

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Ad al-Baghdadi say: Junayd was asked about al-Latif, and he said: He is the one who is gentle with His friends until they know Him and worship Him, and if He were gentle with His enemies they would not deny Him.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Kattani said: Al-Latif is toward whoever of His servants takes refuge in Him, when he despairs of creation; he relies upon Him and returns to Him, and then He accepts him and turns toward him. On this meaning Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi recited to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to me, saying: my father recited to me, saying: Abu 'Ali Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi recited to me:

"Command to empty the graves, as if I / were a man of discernment, and the reward in it is slight. / Whoever God splits his mouth, He decrees his provision; / and my Lord is gentle with whoever takes refuge in Him."

It was also said: al-Latif is He who spreads among His servants the virtues, and conceals their faults. It was said: He is the One who accepts little and gives much. It was said: He is the One who mends the broken and eases the difficult. It was said: He is the One such that no one despairs in this world of His provision, and no believer despairs of His mercy in pardon.

It was said: He is the One whom none fears but His justice, and none hopes for but His bounty. It was said: He is the One who gives His servant blessing beyond his aspiration and imposes obedience within his capacity. It was said: He is the One who does not hasten punishment upon the one who disobeys Him, and does not disappoint the one who hopes in Him. It was said: He is the One who does not turn away His petitioner and does not despair his hopeful. It was said: He is the One who pardons whoever errs. It was said: He is the One who has mercy on whoever has no mercy on himself. It was said: He is the One who helps in service and then increases praise. It was said: He is the One who kindled, in the secrets of His gnostics, through witnessing, a lamp, and made the straight path their highway, and sent down upon them from the clouds of His goodness a flowing water.

﴿He provides whom He wills﴾, as He wills: whomever He wills with abundance, and whomever He wills with restriction; whomever He wills with little and whomever He wills with much; whomever He wills with lawful, and whomever He wills with unlawful; whomever He wills in ease and tranquility, and whomever He wills in toil and hardship; whomever He wills in his own land, and whomever He wills in exile; whomever He wills with reckoning, and whomever He wills without reckoning. ﴿And He is the Strong, the Mighty.﴾

﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter﴾, that is, desires by his deed the Hereafter, ﴿We increase for him in his tilth﴾ by multiplication, by ten for one, up to whatever increase God wills. ﴿And whoever desires the tilth of this world﴾, that is, desires by his deed this world, ﴿We give him of it, but he has no share in the Hereafter.﴾

Qatadah said: He says: whoever works for his Hereafter, ﴿We increase for him in his tilth﴾. And whoever prefers his worldly life over his Hereafter, God does not give him a share in the Hereafter except the Fire, and he does not obtain from the world except the provision that has been finished and apportioned to him.

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed me, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shadhan informed us, al-Husayn ibn Idris informed us, Suwayd ibn Nasr informed us, 'Abd ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Abu Sinan al-Shaybani, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) said: The deeds are of four kinds: a righteous doer on the path of guidance who desires by it the world, for him there is nothing in the Hereafter; that is because God, Exalted, said: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will repay them for their deeds therein﴾ [Surah Hud: 15], the verse. And the one who does for show has no reward in this world or the Hereafter except woe. And a righteous doer on the path of guidance who seeks by it the face of God and the abode of the Hereafter: for him is Paradise in the Hereafter, with its blessing in this world. And a doer of error and sins: his reward is the punishment of God, unless He pardons, for He is the One deserving of piety and the One deserving of forgiveness.

﴿Or do they have partners who have legislated for them of religion what God has not permitted?﴾ ﴿And had it not been for the decisive word﴾, the Day of Resurrection, when He said: ﴿Rather, the Hour is their appointed time﴾ [Surah al-Qamar: 46], ﴿the matter would have been decided between them. And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿You will see the wrongdoers, the polytheists, on the Day of Resurrection, apprehensive﴾, trembling, ﴿because of what they earned, and it will befall them﴾, that is, it will descend upon them inevitably. ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the meadows of the gardens; they will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty.﴾

There is no argument﴾, that is, no dispute, ﴿between us and you.﴾ It was abrogated by the verse of fighting. ﴿God will gather us together﴾ for the final judgment between us. ﴿And to Him is the final return.﴾ ﴿And those who argue concerning God﴾, that is, dispute about the religion of God and His Prophet, ﴿after He has been responded to﴾, that is, after people responded to him, so they became Muslims and entered his religion, because of the manifestation of his miracle and the establishment of his proof, ﴿their argument is baseless﴾, false and vanishing.

﴿With their Lord, and upon them is anger, and for them is a severe punishment.﴾ Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning the Jews and the Christians. They said: our Book is before your Book, our Prophet is before your Prophet, and we are better than you and more deserving of the truth.

Mujahid said: it is that by which weighing is done; and the meaning of the sending down of the balance is God's inspiring creatures to act by it, and His commanding justice and fairness, as in His saying: ﴿We have sent down to you clothing﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 26].

Alqamah said: the balance is Muhammad (ﷺ), who judges between them by the Book.

﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it﴾, supposing that it will not come. ﴿And those who believe are apprehensive of it﴾, fearful of it. ﴿And they know that it is the truth. Unquestionably, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in far error.﴾

Muqatil: Subtle toward the righteous and the wicked among them, in that He does not kill them with hunger because of their sins. al-Qurazi: Subtle with them in the presentation and the reckoning.

al-Khawafi said: Tomorrow, with the Master of creation, there is a standing for creation in which the Majestic One will question them, and the Truthful One is gentle with them concerning provision in two respects: first, that He made your provision from the good things; and second, that He did not give it to you all at once. It was also said: contentment in multiplication. al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl: in the Qur'an and its facilitation.

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: I heard Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Ad al-Baghdadi say: Junayd was asked about al-Latif, and he said: He is the one who is gentle with His friends until they know Him and worship Him, and if He were gentle with His enemies they would not deny Him.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Kattani said: Al-Latif is toward whoever of His servants takes refuge in Him, when he despairs of creation; he relies upon Him and returns to Him, and then He accepts him and turns toward him. On this meaning Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi recited to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to me, saying: my father recited to me, saying: Abu 'Ali Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi recited to me:

"Command to empty the graves, as if I / were a man of discernment, and the reward in it is slight. / Whoever God splits his mouth, He decrees his provision; / and my Lord is gentle with whoever takes refuge in Him."

It was also said: al-Latif is He who spreads among His servants the virtues, and conceals their faults. It was said: He is the One who accepts little and gives much. It was said: He is the One who mends the broken and eases the difficult. It was said: He is the One such that no one despairs in this world of His provision, and no believer despairs of His mercy in pardon.

It was said: He is the One whom none fears but His justice, and none hopes for but His bounty. It was said: He is the One who gives His servant blessing beyond his aspiration and imposes obedience within his capacity. It was said: He is the One who does not hasten punishment upon the one who disobeys Him, and does not disappoint the one who hopes in Him. It was said: He is the One who does not turn away His petitioner and does not despair his hopeful. It was said: He is the One who pardons whoever errs. It was said: He is the One who has mercy on whoever has no mercy on himself. It was said: He is the One who helps in service and then increases praise. It was said: He is the One who kindled, in the secrets of His gnostics, through witnessing, a lamp, and made the straight path their highway, and sent down upon them from the clouds of His goodness a flowing water.

﴿He provides whom He wills﴾, as He wills: whomever He wills with abundance, and whomever He wills with restriction; whomever He wills with little and whomever He wills with much; whomever He wills with lawful, and whomever He wills with unlawful; whomever He wills in ease and tranquility, and whomever He wills in toil and hardship; whomever He wills in his own land, and whomever He wills in exile; whomever He wills with reckoning, and whomever He wills without reckoning. ﴿And He is the Strong, the Mighty.﴾

And the one who does for show has no reward in this world or the Hereafter except woe. And a righteous doer on the path of guidance who seeks by it the face of God and the abode of the Hereafter: for him is Paradise in the Hereafter, with its blessing in this world. And a doer of error and sins: his reward is the punishment of God, unless He pardons, for He is the One deserving of piety and the One deserving of forgiveness.

﴿Or do they have partners who have legislated for them of religion what God has not permitted?﴾ ﴿And had it not been for the decisive word﴾, the Day of Resurrection, when He said: ﴿Rather, the Hour is their appointed time﴾ [Surah al-Qamar: 46], ﴿the matter would have been decided between them. And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿You will see the wrongdoers, the polytheists, on the Day of Resurrection, apprehensive﴾, trembling, ﴿because of what they earned, and it will befall them﴾, that is, it will descend upon them inevitably. ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the meadows of the gardens; they will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty.﴾

The commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 42, verses 8–22:

﴿If God had willed, He would have made them one community upon one religion.﴾ But ﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy; and the wrongdoers, the disbelievers, have no protector or helper.﴾ Or have they taken protectors besides Him? ﴿God is the Protector, and none other.﴾ ﴿He gives life to the dead﴾, meaning, by way of metaphor (majaz): because He gives life to the dead. ﴿He has power over all things﴾, in religion.

﴿Whatever you differ about, its judgment rests with God.﴾ ﴿That is God, my Lord. In Him I have put my trust, and to Him I turn back.﴾ ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth. He made for you mates from among yourselves﴾, meaning spouses (halā'il). He said "from among yourselves" because He created Eve from a rib of Adam. ﴿And of the cattle, mates; He multiplies you thereby﴾, meaning He creates you and sustains you, ﴿therein﴾, that is, in the womb. It was also said: in the belly; it was also said: in the soul; and it was said: in this manner of creation.

Mujahid said: offspring after offspring, and "of the cattle." It was also said that "fi" here means "bi" (with), i.e., He multiplies you by means of it. Ibn Kaysan said: He increases you in number.

﴿There is nothing like Him.﴾ The word "mithl" (like) is here superfluous (silah), and its meaning is: ﴿there is nothing like Him﴾ as "laysa kahuwa shay'" (there is nothing as He is). The word "mithl" was introduced for the emphasis of the statement, as in His saying: ﴿So if they believe in the like of what you believe, they are guided﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 137]. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "fa-in āmanū bi-mā āmantum bihi" (if they believe in what you believe). And Aws ibn Hajar said:

"And slain men like the trunks of palm trees, / over whom falls a pouring rain."

That is, "like trunks." And [another] — so it appears — Sa'd ibn Zayd said:

"When I see their excellence, / there is none among the people like them."

And another said:

"There is none like al-Fata Zuhayr, / a character that equals him in virtues."

It was also said that the "ka" (like) is superfluous (silah), and its meaning is: "laysa mithlahu" (there is nothing like him), as the rajaz poet said:

"And hearths like the stones [of the cooking pot]..."

So he added a second "ka" to the "ka" for the emphasis of the comparison. Another said:

"[The swift ones] drive away the shining horses on the road, / a slender [mare] like an egg in a nest."

Here he combined "ka" with "'an".

﴿And He is the Hearing, the Seeing.﴾ ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. He extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it.﴾ ﴿Indeed, He is Knower of all things.﴾ ﴿He has prescribed for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah﴾, and he is the first of the prophets of the Law (shari'ah).

﴿And what We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus﴾: they differed concerning the sense of this verse. Qatadah said: the permitting of the lawful and the forbidding of the unlawful. al-Hakam said: the forbidding of sisters, mothers and daughters. Mujahid said: God did not send any prophet without enjoining upon him the establishment of prayer, the giving of zakat, and acknowledgment of obedience to God.

﴿That is His religion which He prescribed for them﴾. This is the narration of al-Wali from Ibn 'Abbas. It was also said: the religion is monotheism (tawhid). It was also said: it is His saying ﴿that you establish the religion and do not divide over it﴾. All the prophets were sent to establish the religion, unity, community, and to abandon division and opposition. ﴿Hard upon the polytheists is what you call them to﴾, of monotheism and the rejection of idols. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿God chooses for Himself whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns back﴾, that is, He singles him out for His religion.

﴿And they did not divide﴾, meaning the people of the differing religions. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means the People of the Book. Its proof and parallel is in surah al-Bayyinah: ﴿except after clear evidence had come to them﴾ [Surah al-Bayyinah: 4].

﴿except after knowledge had come to them﴾, that is, before the sending of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his description. ﴿Out of envy among themselves.﴾ ﴿Had not a word preceded from your Lord﴾, the delay of punishment, ﴿until an appointed term﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾ by punishment.

﴿And indeed, those who were given the Book after them﴾, meaning after the earlier nations. Mujahid said: its meaning is "before them", that is, before the polytheists of Makkah, namely the Jews and the Christians. ﴿Are in disquieting doubt about it﴾. ﴿So for that, call﴾, as in His saying: ﴿because your Lord has inspired her﴾ [Surah al-Zalzalah: 5], that is, to it; i.e., to that to which those given the Book were called. ﴿And be steadfast as you were commanded﴾, that is, persist in the religion with which you were commanded. ﴿And do not follow their desires. And say: I believe in what God has sent down of Book, and I was commanded to do justice among you﴾, that is, that I should be just, or in order that I may be just, as in His saying: ﴿and we were commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 71].

Ibn 'Abbas said: that I may make you equal in religion, and that I believe in every Book and every Messenger. Others said: ﴿to do justice among you﴾ in all circumstances and affairs.

Qatadah said: The Prophet of God (ﷺ) was commanded to be just, and he was just until he died, and justice is the balance of God on earth.

It has been related to us that Dawud (peace be upon him) said: Three qualities, whoever has them is the winner: moderation in wealth and poverty, justice in contentment and anger, and goodness in secret and in public. That is what I mentioned of the bliss of the Gardens. Allah gives good news of it to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds; indeed, they are its people.

﴿Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it, except affection for kinship.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came from Makkah to Madinah, he was subject to calamities and obligations, and he had no means to meet them. The Ansar said: "This man, whom Allah has guided us through, is the son of our sister, and his calamities are ours." So they said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, you are the son of our sister, Allah guided us through your hands, and calamities and obligations befall you while you have no means for them. We think we should gather some of our wealth for you, bring it to you, and you may use it for what befalls you." And here it is. Then this verse was revealed.

Qatadah said: The polytheists gathered in an assembly, and some of them said to others: "Do you think Muhammad asks a reward for what he undertakes?" So Allah revealed this verse, urging them to love him and to love his relatives.

This interpretation is closer to the apparent meaning of the verse and its revelation, since this surah is Meccan. Scholars differed about the meaning of the verse.

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed us, reading it to him, that 'Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi told us: Abu Bakr al-Azdi told us: 'Asim ibn 'Ali told us: Qaza'ah ibn Suwayd told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "I do not ask you a reward for what I have brought you of clear signs and guidance, except that you love Allah and draw near to Him through obedience to Him." [170] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/268; al-Mustadrak: 2/444.]]

Al-Hasan al-Basri held this view and said: It means nearness to Allah. It says: "Except drawing near to Allah and seeking His love through obedience and righteous deeds."

Tawus, al-Sha'bi, al-Walibi and al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: There was no clan of Quraysh except that the Messenger of Allah had kinship with them. When they denied him and refused to pledge allegiance to him, Allah revealed: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for kinship﴾, meaning: that you protect me, love me, and maintain the ties of kinship with me. The Messenger of Allah said: "If you refuse to pledge allegiance to me, then protect my kinship among you and do not harm me, for you are my people and the most deserving of those who obey me and respond to me." [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 25/31.]] [171]

Abu Malik, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd and Qatadah held this view. Others said: Its meaning is: except that you love my relatives and my lineage, and protect me concerning them. This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb.

Then they differed about the relatives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) whose love Allah commanded.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh al-Thaqafi al-'Adl informed us: Burhan ibn 'Ali al-Sufi told us: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman al-Hadrami told us: Harb ibn al-Hasan al-Tahhan told us: Husayn al-Ashqar told us, from Qays, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for kinship﴾ was revealed, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are these relatives of yours whose love is obligatory upon us?"

He said: "'Ali, Fatimah and their two sons." [[Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/103.]] [172]

The evidence for this interpretation is what

Abu Mansur al-Jamshadhi informed us, saying: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz told me: Abu Bakr ibn Malik told me: Muhammad ibn Yunus told us: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'A'ishah told us: Isma'il ibn 'Amr told us, from 'Umar ibn Musa, from Zayd ibn 'Ali ibn Husayn, from his father, from his grandfather 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "I complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of people's envy of me." He said: "Are you not pleased to be the fourth of four: the first to enter Paradise are I, you, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and our wives on our right and left, and our descendants behind our wives, and our followers behind us?" [173] [[Shawahid al-Tanzil: 1/185.]]

Abu Mansur al-Jamshadhi told us: Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ahmad told us: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Hammam told us: Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Rizin told us: Hassan ibn Hassan told us: Hammad ibn Salamah, the nephew of Humayd al-Tawil, told us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Fatimah: "Bring me your husband and your two sons." She brought them, and he threw over them a Fadak cloak, then raised his hands over them and said: "O Allah, these are the family of Muhammad, so send Your blessings and mercy upon the family of Muhammad, for You are Praiseworthy and Glorious." She said: I lifted the cloak to enter with them, but he pulled it away and said: "You are on good." [174] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/323.]]

Abu Hazim narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and said: "I am at war with whoever wars with you, and at peace with whoever is at peace with you." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 5/360.]] [175]

'Aqil ibn Muhammad informed us: al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya ibn al-Mubtali informed us: Muhammad ibn Jarir told us: Muhammad ibn 'Umarah told me: Isma'il ibn Aban told us: al-Sabbah ibn Yahya al-Muzani told us, from al-Suddi, from Abu al-Daylam, who said: When 'Ali ibn al-Husayn was brought as a captive and placed on the steps of Damascus, a man of the people of Syria stood up and said: "Praise be to Allah who killed you, uprooted you, and cut off the horn of sedition." 'Ali ibn al-Husayn said: "Have you read the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Have you read Ha Mim?" He said: "I have read the Qur'an, but I have not read Ha Mim." He said: "Have you not read ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for kinship﴾?" He said: "And are you truly those?" He said: "Yes." [176]

Al-Husayn ibn al-'Alawi al-Wasi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahdi told us: my father told me: 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida told us: my father Musa ibn Ja'far told me: my father Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq told us, saying:

The engraving on the ring of my father Abu Muhammad ibn 'Ali was:

My trust in Allah is good,
And in the Prophet, the trusted,
And in the executor, possessor of favours,
And in al-Husayn and al-Hasan.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Mawardi recited to us; Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Za'farani recited to me; Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Jurjani recited to me, saying: Mansur al-Faqih recited to me, for himself:

If my love is for five,
Through them my obligations are purified,
And hatred for those who oppose them
Is rejection, for I am a rejecter. [[Jawahir al-'Iqdayn: 2/304; Yanabi' al-Mawaddah: 3/103.]]

It was also said: They are the descendants of 'Abd al-Muttalib. What supports this is

Abu al-'Abbas Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Marwazi told us: Abu al-Hasan al-Mahmudi told us: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Arsabandi told us: Hadiyyah ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab told us: Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far told us: 'Abd Allah ibn Ziyad al-Yamami told us, from Ishaq ibn Abi 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We are the descendants of 'Abd al-Muttalib, the lords of the people of Paradise: I, Hamzah, Ja'far, 'Ali, al-Hasan, al-Husayn and al-Mahdi." [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1368.]] [177]

'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida: my father Musa ibn Ja'far told me: my father Ja'far ibn Muhammad told me: my father Muhammad ibn 'Ali told me: my father 'Ali ibn al-Husayn told me, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Paradise is forbidden to whoever wrongs my Household and harms me concerning my family. And whoever does a favour to anyone of the descendants of 'Abd al-Muttalib and is not repaid for it, I will repay him tomorrow when he meets me on the Day of Resurrection." [178] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/22.]]

It was also said: They are those for whom sadaqah (charity) is forbidden and among whom the khums (one-fifth) is distributed, namely the Banu Hashim and the Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib who committed no sin in the Jahiliyyah or in Islam. The evidence is His saying: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, one-fifth of it belongs to Allah, to the Messenger, and to the near of kin﴾, [[Surah al-Anfal: 41.]] and His saying: ﴿What Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah, to the Messenger, and to the near of kin﴾, [[Surah al-Hashr: 7.]] and His saying: ﴿And give the near of kin his right﴾. [[Surah al-Isra': 17.]]

'Aqil ibn Muhammad informed us by license: Abu al-Faraj al-Baghdadi informed us: Muhammad ibn Judayr told us: Abu Kurayb told us: Malik ibn Isma'il told us: 'Abd al-Salam told us, saying: Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad told me, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Ansar said: "We did this and we did that," as if they were reproaching him. Ibn 'Abbas, or al-'Abbas, said: "'Abd al-Salam..." [the transmission is corrupt here] ... they had favour over you. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he came to them in their gatherings and said: "O assembly of the Ansar, were you not humble, and did Allah not honour you through me?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Were you not misguided, and did Allah not guide you through me?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Will you not answer me?" They said: "What should we say, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Will you not say: Did your people not drive you out and we sheltered you? Did they not deny you and we believed you? Did they not forsake you and we helped you?"

He kept saying this until they fell on their knees and said: "Our wealth and what is in our hands belongs to Allah and His Messenger." Then there was revealed: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, except affection for kinship﴾. [179] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 25/33.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamzah told us: 'Ubayd ibn Sharik al-Bazzaz told us: Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, the grandson of Shurahbil's daughter, told us: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah al-Fazari told us: Yahya ibn Bishr al-Asadi told us, from Salih ibn Hayyan al-Fazari, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Hadi, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the matter with Quraysh? Some of them meet others with faces that almost drip with affection, but they meet us with faces that are stern and frowning." The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Do they do that?" He said: "Yes, by Him who sent you with the truth." He said: "By Him who sent me with the truth, they will not believe until they love you for my sake." [180] [[al-Musannaf: 7/518; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 11/343; Kanz al-'Ummal: 13/514.]]

Some people said: This verse is abrogated (mansukhah) by naskh (abrogation). It was revealed in Makkah, when the polytheists were harming the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah revealed this verse commanding them to love the Messenger of Allah and maintain his kinship. When he emigrated to Madinah and the Ansar sheltered him, supported him and helped him, Allah wished to join him with his brother prophets (peace be upon them), who said: ﴿And I do not ask you any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾. [[Surah al-Shu'ara': 109.]] So Allah revealed to him: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours; my reward is only from Allah﴾. [[Surah Saba': 47.]] Therefore it is abrogated by this verse, and by His saying: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, and I am not of those who pretend﴾, [[Surah Sad: 86.]] and His saying: ﴿And you ask them no reward for it; it is only a reminder to the worlds﴾, [[Surah al-Mu'minun: 72.]] and His saying: ﴿Or do you ask them for payment? But the payment of your Lord is better﴾, [[Surah Yusuf: 104.]] and His saying: ﴿Or do you ask them for a reward, so they are burdened with debt?﴾ [[Surah al-Tur: 40.]] This was the view of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim and al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl.

This view is neither strong nor acceptable, because none of the interpretations we have related of this verse can be abrogated. It is enough of a victory against the one who claims that drawing near to Allah through obedience to Him and love for His Prophet and his Household is abrogated.

The proof of the correctness of our position on it is what

Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed us: Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Balkhi informed us: Ya'qub ibn Yusuf ibn Ishaq told us: Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Tusi told us: Ya'la ibn 'Ubayd told us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies loving the family of Muhammad dies as a martyr. Indeed, whoever dies loving the family of Muhammad dies forgiven. Indeed, whoever dies loving the family of Muhammad dies repentant. Indeed, whoever dies loving the family of Muhammad dies a believer with complete faith. Indeed, whoever dies loving the family of Muhammad, the Angel of Death gives him the good news of Paradise, then Munkar and Nakir. Indeed, whoever dies loving the family of Muhammad, Allah makes the visitors of his grave the angels of the Most Merciful. Indeed, whoever dies loving the family of Muhammad, two gates to Paradise are opened for him in his grave. Indeed, whoever dies hating the family of Muhammad will come on the Day of Resurrection with 'Despairing of Allah's mercy' written between his eyes. Indeed, whoever dies hating the family of Muhammad dies a disbeliever. Indeed, whoever dies hating the family of Muhammad will not smell the fragrance of Paradise." [181] [[Yanabi' al-Mawaddah: 3/140; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/23, with slight variation.]]

﴿And whoever commits a good deed﴾ means: whoever earns obedience. ﴿We will increase for him therein in goodness﴾ by multiplication. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn Hanash al-Muqri told us: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl told us: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn told us: Isma'il ibn Musa told us: al-Hakam ibn Tahr told us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And whoever commits a good deed, We will increase for him therein in goodness﴾, he said: "The love of the family of Muhammad (ﷺ)." [[al-'Umdah of Ibn Bitriq, from the author: p. 55, hadith 53; Nazm Durar al-Simtayn: 86; al-Kamil of Ibn 'Adi: 2/209, biography of al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr al-Farazi.]]

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against Allah"?﴾ (The reference is to the disbelievers of Makkah.)

﴿If Allah willed, He would seal your heart.﴾

Mujahid said: this means He would bind your heart with patience, so that their harm would not weigh heavily on you. Qatadah said: this means He would set a seal upon your heart so that you would forget the Qur'an. So He informed them that if he had invented a lie against Allah, He would have done to him what He mentioned in the verse.

Then He began, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And Allah will erase falsehood﴾. Al-Kisa'i said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it.

Its meaning is: Allah erases falsehood. The waw was omitted in the Mushaf, though it is in the nominative position, just as it was omitted in His saying ﴿And man prays﴾ [Al-Isra 17:11] and ﴿We shall call the guards of Hell﴾ [Al-Alaq 96:18], following the pronunciation.

﴿And establishes the truth by His words.﴾ [.......] [blank space in the manuscript]. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts.﴾

Ibn Abbas said:

When ﴿I do not ask you for it any reward﴾ [Ash-Shura 42:23] was revealed, something of it entered the hearts of some people, and they said: "He wants nothing except to urge us toward his relatives after him." Then they left, and Jibril (peace be upon him) descended and informed him that they had accused him, and revealed this verse. The people said: "O Messenger of Allah, we testify that you are truthful." So He revealed ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾.

The expressions of the scholars differed regarding the reality of repentance (tawbah, turning back to Allah) and its conditions.

Al-Imam Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Habib informed us by reading it to me, in the months of the year 388 (AH), saying: Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Mansur narrated to us, Muhammad Miskan ibn Jabalah of Sawah narrated to us.

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Dawud informed us, from Ibrahim ibn Tahman, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: A Bedouin entered the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Allah, I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You," quickly, and he said Allahu akbar. When he finished his prayer, Ali said to him: "O man, quickness of the tongue in seeking forgiveness is the repentance of liars, and your repentance needs repentance." He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, what is repentance?" He said: "It is a term that falls upon six meanings: regret for the past sins, returning to make up what was neglected of the obligatory duties, restoring what was unjustly taken, melting the self in obedience just as you melted it in disobedience, making the self taste the bitterness of obedience just as you tasted the sweetness of disobedience, and weeping in place of every laugh you laughed."

I heard al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan say: I heard Ibrahim ibn Yazid say: I heard Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Tirmidhi say: It was said to Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Warraq: "When does a man become a penitent (ta'ib)?"

He said: "When he returns to Allah, watching Him, feeling shame before Him, fearing His vengeance regarding what he disobeyed Him in, clinging to His mercy and hoping in it, remembering His forbearance in concealing (his sins) so that it makes him weep, regretting what displeasing thing came to him, thanking his Lord for what came to him, understanding Allah's admonition and retaining it, and preserving His covenant regarding what He enjoined upon him."

I heard al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Habib say: I heard Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sum'an al-Mudhakkir say: I heard Abu Bakr ibn al-Shah, the Persian Sufi, say: Al-Harith ibn Asad al-Muhasibi was asked: "Who is the penitent?" He said: "He who sees himself as protected from sins and guided to good deeds, sees the joy absent from his heart and sorrow remaining in it, is loved by the people of goodness and feared by the people of evil, sees little of the world as much, sees much of the work of the Hereafter as little, and sees his heart empty of everything guaranteed to him, occupied with everything he was commanded."

Al-Sari ibn al-Mughallis al-Saqati said: Repentance is the sincerity of resolve to abandon sins, turning of the heart in repentance to the Knower of the unseen, regret over what has passed of defects, and thorough self-accounting with humility and submission.

Amr ibn Uthman said: The foundation of repentance is correcting one's sustenance (i.e., making one's earnings lawful).

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Babi say: I heard Abu Ya'la Hamzah ibn Wahb al-Tabari say: I heard al-Hasan ibn Alawiyyah al-Damghani say: I heard Yahya ibn Mu'adh, when he was asked: "Who is the penitent?" He said: "He who breaks his youth over his head, breaks the world over the head of Satan, and clings to weaning until death comes to him."

Sahl ibn Abdullah said: Repentance is the transition from blameworthy states to praiseworthy states. Ibn al-Hasan al-Bushaykhi was asked about repentance, and he said: "When you remember a sin, you do not find its sweetness in your heart."

Al-Ra'i said: Repentance is abandoning sins, in intention and in action, and turning to obedience, in intention and in action. I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Imad al-Baghdadi say: Al-Junayd was asked: "Who is the penitent?"

He said: "He who repents from what is other than Allah."

Shah al-Kirmani [died 270 AH; his name is Shah ibn Shuja al-Kirmani, Abu al-Fawaris; see al-Wafi, 14/23] said: "Leave the world, for you have repented; oppose your desire, for you have arrived."

And He pardons the evil deeds of those who repent, so He erases them.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ja'far informed us, my father narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Sawad narrated to us, Atiyyah ibn Lafthah narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-Zubayri narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah.

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted is more pleased with the repentance of His believing servant than with one who is lost and finds (his way), than with a barren woman who bears a child, and than with one who is thirsty and reaches water. Whoever repents to Allah the Exalted with sincere repentance, Allah makes his two guardian angels forget his sins, and the places on earth forget his errors and sins." Or he said: "his sins and his errors." [182]

﴿And He knows what you do.﴾ Al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read it with the ta' (taa, "you"), and it is the reading of Abdullah and his companions. The narration of Hafs from Asim, other than them, reads it with the ya' (yaa, "He"), and it is the choice of Abu Ubayd, who said: "Because it refers to those whom He spoke of: ﴿His servants﴾ was mentioned before it, and ﴿And He increases them of His bounty﴾ after it."

﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, that is, obeys those who believe, their Lord, according to the saying of some of them.

Others made the action belong to God: ﴿And Allah responds to those who believe﴾, making the response an act of Allah the Exalted. This is more correct and more pleasing to me, because it occurs between two actions of Allah the Exalted: the first is His saying ﴿He accepts﴾, and the second is ﴿And He increases them of His bounty﴾. The meaning of the verse is: Allah answers the believers when they call upon Him. It was also said: its meaning is: We answer the supplication of believers for one another.

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, Makki ibn Abdan informed us, Abdullah ibn Hashim narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah ibn al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shaqiq ibn Salamah, from Salamah ibn Sabrah, who said: Mu'adh (ibn Jabal) addressed us in Syria, saying: "You are the believers and you are the people of Paradise. By Allah, I hope that those whom you revile from Persia and Rome will enter Paradise, and that is because one of them, when he does a deed for one of you, you say: 'You have done well, may Allah have mercy on you, you have done well, may Allah bless you,' and Allah the Glorified and Exalted says: ﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds, and increases them of His bounty﴾. ﴿But the disbelievers will have a severe punishment﴾."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us, al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi narrated to me, Abu Ahmad Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Zaffarani al-Hamadhani narrated to me, Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Qutaybah narrated to us in Asqalan, Muhammad ibn Ayyub ibn Suwayd narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas regarding the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, he said: "He intercedes for them on behalf of their brothers." ﴿And increases them of His bounty﴾. He said: "For the brothers of their brothers."

﴿And if Allah had extended provision for His servants﴾. The verse was revealed concerning a group of the people of the Suffah (the poor companions who lived in the mosque) who wished for the abundance and wealth of the world. Khabbab ibn Lādin said: "This verse was revealed concerning us, because we looked at the Banu Qurayzah, al-Nadir, and Banu Qaynuqa', and we wished for it. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And if Allah had extended﴾, that is, had expanded provision for His servants."

﴿They would have transgressed in the earth﴾, that is, they would have become insolent and disobedient. Ibn Abbas said: "Their transgression is injustice: one station after another, one mount after another, one vehicle after another, one garment after another."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tabsitani al-Isfahani informed us, Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Abbas al-Usmi al-Harawi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn informed me, Ahmad ibn Salih al-Karabisi narrated to us, saying: I heard Qusayr ibn Yahya say: Shaqiq ibn Ibrahim said regarding the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And if Allah had extended provision for His servants, they would have transgressed﴾, he said: "If Allah provided the servants without any earning, and they were free from livelihood and earning, they would have become insolent in the earth, transgressed, and striven in the earth for corruption. But He occupied them with earning and livelihood out of His mercy and favor."

﴿But He sends down in measure what He wills﴾. Their provisions are sent down in the measure He wills, for their sufficiency. Muqatil said: ﴿But He sends down in measure what He wills﴾, so He made one poor and another rich.

﴿Indeed He is, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing﴾. Qatadah said: "In this verse it was said: the best provision is that which neither makes you rebellious nor distracts you."

It has also been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What I fear most for my nation is the splendor of the world and its abundance." [183]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah narrated to us, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Ghaffar al-Zarqani narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Azdi narrated to us, Abu Hafs Umar ibn Sa'id al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Sadaqah ibn Abdullah narrated to us, Abd al-Karim al-Jazari narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), from Jibril (peace be upon him), from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, who said: "Whoever humiliates a friend of Mine has declared war against Me. I am swiftest to aid My friends, and I become angry for them as a lion becomes furious. I do not hesitate in anything I do as I hesitate in taking the soul of My believing servant: he dislikes death, and I dislike harming him, yet it is inevitable for him. [In the source: 'Nothing draws My servant closer to Me than the performance of what I have obligated upon him, and My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts until I love him.'] When I love him, I am his hearing, his sight, his tongue, and his hand, and one who supports him. If he asks Me, I give him; if he calls upon Me, I respond to him. Among My believing servants is one who would ask Me for a door of worship, and if I gave it to him, vanity would enter him and ruin him. Among My believing servants is one whom only sickness will reform, and if I healed him, that would ruin him. Among My believing servants is one whom only health will reform, and if I afflicted him with sickness, that would ruin him. Among My believing servants is one whom only wealth will reform, and if I made him poor, that would ruin him. Among My believing servants is one whom only poverty will reform, and if I made him rich, that would ruin him. Indeed I manage My servants, knowing their hearts. Indeed I am Knowing, Acquainted." [Tafsir al-Qurtubi, 16/28]

Sadaqah said: I heard Aban ibn Abi Ayyash narrate this hadith from Anas ibn Malik, and then he would say: "O Allah, I am among Your believing servants whom only wealth will reform, so do not make me poor."

﴿And it is He who sends down the rain﴾, meaning the rain. It was so named because it brings relief (yughithu) to people, that is, it protects them and sets their affairs right.

Al-Asma'i said: I passed by some tribes of the Arabs who had been given rain, and I asked an old woman among them: "How much rain has come to you?" She said: "It has brought us relief as much as we wished" (ghathana ma shi'na).

﴿After they had despaired, and spreads His mercy﴾, that is, spreads His rain. A parallel to it is His saying: ﴿And He it is who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy﴾ [Al-A'raf 7:57].

Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad informed us, Abu al-Azhar informed us, Rawh narrated to us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that a man came to Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, the rain has been withheld and people have despaired."

He said: "You have been given rain." Then he recited: ﴿And He it is who sends down the rain after they had despaired, and spreads His mercy.﴾

﴿And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy.﴾

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against Allah"?﴾ (The reference is to the disbelievers of Makkah.)

﴿If Allah willed, He would seal your heart.﴾

Mujahid said: this means He would bind your heart with patience, so that their harm would not weigh heavily on you. Qatadah said: this means He would set a seal upon your heart so that you would forget the Qur'an. So He informed them that if he had invented a lie against Allah, He would have done to him what He mentioned in the verse.

﴿And establishes the truth by His words.﴾ [.......] [blank space in the manuscript]. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts.﴾

When ﴿I do not ask you for it any reward﴾ [Ash-Shura 42:23] was revealed, something of it entered the hearts of some people, and they said: "He wants nothing except to urge us toward his relatives after him." The people said: "O Messenger of Allah, we testify that you are truthful." So He revealed ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾.

I heard al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Habib say: I heard Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sum'an al-Mudhakkir say: I heard Abu Bakr ibn al-Shah, the Persian Sufi, say: Al-Harith ibn Asad al-Muhasibi was asked: "Who is the penitent?" He said: "He who sees himself as protected from sins and guided to good deeds, sees the joy absent from his heart and sorrow remaining in it, is loved by the people of goodness and feared by the people of evil, sees little of the world as much, sees much of the work of the Hereafter as little, and sees his heart empty of everything guaranteed to him, occupied with everything he was commanded."

Al-Sari ibn al-Mughallis al-Saqati said: Repentance is the sincerity of resolve to abandon sins, turning of the heart in repentance to the Knower of the unseen, regret over what has passed of defects, and thorough self-accounting with humility and submission.

Amr ibn Uthman said: The foundation of repentance is correcting one's sustenance (i.e., making one's earnings lawful).

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Babi say: I heard Abu Ya'la Hamzah ibn Wahb al-Tabari say: I heard al-Hasan ibn Alawiyyah al-Damghani say: I heard Yahya ibn Mu'adh, when he was asked: "Who is the penitent?" He said: "He who breaks his youth over his head, breaks the world over the head of Satan, and clings to weaning until death comes to him."

Sahl ibn Abdullah said: Repentance is the transition from blameworthy states to praiseworthy states. Ibn al-Hasan al-Bushaykhi was asked about repentance, and he said: "When you remember a sin, you do not find its sweetness in your heart."

Al-Ra'i said: Repentance is abandoning sins, in intention and in action, and turning to obedience, in intention and in action. I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Imad al-Baghdadi say: Al-Junayd was asked: "Who is the penitent?"

He said: "He who repents from what is other than Allah."

Shah al-Kirmani [died 270 AH; his name is Shah ibn Shuja al-Kirmani, Abu al-Fawaris; see al-Wafi, 14/23] said: "Leave the world, for you have repented; oppose your desire, for you have arrived."

And He pardons the evil deeds of those who repent, so He erases them.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ja'far informed us, my father narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Sawad narrated to us, Atiyyah ibn Lafthah narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-Zubayri narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah.

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted is more pleased with the repentance of His believing servant than with one who is lost and finds (his way), than with a barren woman who bears a child, and than with one who is thirsty and reaches water. Whoever repents to Allah the Exalted with sincere repentance, Allah makes his two guardian angels forget his sins, and the places on earth forget his errors and sins." Or he said: "his sins and his errors." [182]

﴿And He knows what you do.﴾ Al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read it with the ta' (taa, "you"), and it is the reading of Abdullah and his companions. ﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, that is, obeys those who believe, their Lord, according to the saying of some of them.

Others made the action belong to God: ﴿And Allah responds to those who believe﴾, making the response an act of Allah the Exalted. He said: "For the brothers of their brothers."

﴿And if Allah had extended provision for His servants﴾. The verse was revealed concerning a group of the people of the Suffah (the poor companions who lived in the mosque) who wished for the abundance and wealth of the world. ﴿They would have transgressed in the earth﴾, that is, they would have become insolent and disobedient. Ibn Abbas said: "Their transgression is injustice: one station after another, one mount after another, one vehicle after another, one garment after another."

But He occupied them with earning and livelihood out of His mercy and favor."

﴿But He sends down in measure what He wills﴾. Their provisions are sent down in the measure He wills, for their sufficiency. Muqatil said: ﴿But He sends down in measure what He wills﴾, so He made one poor and another rich.

I am swiftest to aid My friends, and I become angry for them as a lion becomes furious. I do not hesitate in anything I do as I hesitate in taking the soul of My believing servant: he dislikes death, and I dislike harming him, yet it is inevitable for him. ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against Allah"?﴾ (The reference is to the disbelievers of Makkah.)

﴿If Allah willed, He would seal your heart.﴾

Mujahid said: this means He would bind your heart with patience, so that their harm would not weigh heavily on you. Qatadah said: this means He would set a seal upon your heart so that you would forget the Qur'an. So He informed them that if he had invented a lie against Allah, He would have done to him what He mentioned in the verse.

Then He began, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And Allah will erase falsehood﴾. Al-Kisa'i said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it.

Its meaning is: Allah erases falsehood. The waw was omitted in the Mushaf, though it is in the nominative position, just as it was omitted in His saying ﴿And man prays﴾ [Al-Isra 17:11] and ﴿We shall call the guards of Hell﴾ [Al-Alaq 96:18], following the pronunciation.

﴿And establishes the truth by His words.﴾ [.......] [blank space in the manuscript]. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts.﴾

Ibn Abbas said:

When ﴿I do not ask you for it any reward﴾ [Ash-Shura 42:23] was revealed, something of it entered the hearts of some people, and they said: "He wants nothing except to urge us toward his relatives after him." Then they left, and Jibril (peace be upon him) descended and informed him that they had accused him, and revealed this verse. The people said: "O Messenger of Allah, we testify that you are truthful." So He revealed ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants﴾.

The expressions of the scholars differed regarding the reality of repentance (tawbah, turning back to Allah) and its conditions.

﴿And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 42, verses 29–37:

﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and of the living creatures He has scattered throughout them. And He is Able to gather them whenever He wills.﴾ ﴿Whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your own hands have earned﴾ — of sins and transgressions. ﴿And He pardons much of it, so He does not take you to account for it.﴾

The people of Madina and Syria read ﴿bi-mā﴾ without the fa' (فاء, "fa", the particle of consequence), and it is so in their codices. The rest read ﴿fa-bi-mā﴾ with the fa', and it is so in their codices too. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this reading.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Muqri informed us: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Yaʿqub related to us: Radwan ibn Ahmad related to us: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar related to us: Abu Muʿawiya al-Darir related to us, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan, who said: When this verse was revealed — ﴿Whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your own hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ — the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No vein throbs, no twig is scratched, and no stone strikes [a person] except because of a sin, and what Allah pardons is more." [184] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/31.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i related to us: Bishr ibn Musa al-Asadi related to us: Khalaf ibn al-Walid related to us: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya related to us: al-Azhar ibn Rashid al-Kahili related to me, from al-Khadir ibn al-Qawwas al-'Ijli, from Abu Sakhila, who said: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu) said:

"Shall I inform you of the best verse in the Book of Allah, which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) related to us: ﴿Whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your own hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾." He said: "And I will explain it to you, O ʿAli: whatever affliction, trial, illness or punishment you suffer in this world, Allah is too generous to repeat the punishment upon you in the Hereafter; and whatever He pardoned in this world, Allah is too forbearing to return after His pardon." [185] [[Musnad Abi Ya'la: 1/352; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 16/30.]]

He said, with his chain, from Khalaf ibn al-Walid, from al-Mubarak ibn Fadala, from al-Hasan, who said: We entered upon ʿImran ibn al-Husayn during his severe illness which had afflicted him. A man among us said: "I must ask you about the pain I see in you." ʿImran said: "O my brother, do not do so, for by Allah, what I love most is what Allah the Exalted loves."
