﴿If He wills, He stills the wind, and they remain motionless upon its surface.﴾ — that is, upon the surface of the water. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for everyone who is steadfast and grateful.﴾ ﴿Or He destroys them for what they have earned﴾ — that is, for what their people and riders have earned of sins. ﴿And He pardons much﴾ — so He does not punish for them, and He knows.

The people of Madina and Syria read ﴿yaʿfu﴾ in the nominative (bi-l-raf') as a new sentence, like His saying in Surat Bara'a: ﴿And Allah accepts repentance from whom He wills﴾ [[Surat al-Tawba: 15.]]. The others read it in the accusative (naṣb) by conjugation (al-ṣarf), like His saying: ﴿And that He may know those who are patient﴾ [[Surat Al ʿImran: 142.]], shifted from the state of jazm (apocope) to naṣb, for propriety and to avoid the heaviness of successive jazm, as in the saying of al-Nabigha:

"If Abu Qabus perishes, the spring of people and the sacred month perish, and we hold after him to the tail of a life whose back is shaved and whose hump is cut off."

And another said:

"Do not forbid a deed while you commit its like; it is a great shame upon you when you do it."

﴿And those who dispute concerning Our signs will know that they will have no escape.﴾ — no refuge from the punishment of Allah the Exalted. ﴿So whatever you have been given is the enjoyment of worldly life﴾ — of the finery and goods of this world, and it is not provision for the Hereafter. ﴿But what is with Allah is better and more lasting for those who believe and rely upon their Lord﴾ — the reward. ﴿And those who avoid the major sins and immoralities.﴾

Yahya ibn Ri'ab, Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read here and in Surat al-Najm ﴿kabīra﴾ (كبير) in the singular, and they explained it as shirk (polytheism) on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas. The rest read ﴿kabā'ira﴾ (كبائر) in the plural in both surahs. We have already explained the scholars' disagreement about the meaning of "major sins" (al-kaba'ir) and "immoralities" (al-fawahish). Al-Suddi said: it means fornication (al-zina). Muqatil said: it means things that necessitate eternal abiding (in Hell).

﴿And when they are angry, they forgive﴾ — they overlook and bear patiently.

And those who answer their Lord, establish prayer, conduct their affairs by mutual consultation, and spend out of what We have provided them. It was said: these verses were revealed about Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, when people blamed him for spending all of his wealth, and when he was insulted and showed forbearance.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba related to us: Ishaq ibn Sadaqa related to us: Abd Allah ibn Hashim related to us: Sayf ibn Umar related to us, from Atiyya, from Ayyub, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Once Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, came into possession of wealth, and he gave all of it in charity for the cause of good. The Muslims blamed him and the disbelievers criticized him, so Allah the Exalted revealed: "So whatever you have been given is but the enjoyment of this worldly life..." up to His words: "and from what We have provided them they spend." He specified it for Abu Bakr and extended it to those who followed him.

And those who, when wrong is inflicted upon them, defend themselves: they take revenge on their oppressors without transgressing.

Muqatil said: this refers to the one who has been wounded, who takes revenge on the one who wounded him and seeks retaliation against him. Ibrahim said: in this verse, they disliked being humiliated, and when they had the power, they pardoned.

"And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it." The recompense is named after the initial act, although it is not an evil, because the two resemble each other in form. Ibn Najih said: it means that the one who utters an ugly word is answered with its like; so if he says, "May Allah disgrace him," the response is, "May Allah disgrace him." Al-Suddi said: if he insults you with an insult, then insult him with its like, without transgressing.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn Hanash the reciter related to us: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl related to us: Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Abi Umar related to us. Sufyan ibn Uyayna said: I said to Sufyan al-Thawri: What is the meaning of His words, "And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it"? Is it that a man insults you and you insult him, or that he does something to you and you do the same to him? He had no answer for me, so I asked Hisham ibn Hujayr about this verse. He said: if a wounder wounds, you retaliate against him; it is not that he curses you and you curse him.

Sufyan said: Ibn Shubruma used to say: "Is there not in Makka someone like Hisham ibn Hujayr?" [He said this] regarding "But whoever pardons and reconciles..." [meaning] one who did not take revenge.

Ibn Abbas said: "whoever gives up retaliation and makes reconciliation." Muqatil said: pardon is among the righteous deeds, so its reward is upon Allah.

Ibn Fanjawayh, the just, said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Bishr related to us; Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Mulas al-Dimashqi informed us; Abu Abd Allah Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Bishr al-Qurashi related to us; Zuhayr ibn Abbad al-Mada'ini related to us; Sufyan ibn Uyayna related to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out: whoever has a reward with Allah, let him stand up." He said: a great multitude will stand up. He said: [Then] it will be said: "What is your reward with Allah?" They will say: "We are those who pardoned those who wronged us." That is His words, "But whoever pardons and reconciles, his reward is upon Allah." Then it will be said to them: "Enter Paradise by the permission of Allah."

Indeed, Allah does not love the wrongdoers. Ibn Abbas said: [They are] those who initiate the wrong, due to His words: "And whoever avenges himself after being wronged, those have no path [of blame] against them. The path is only against those who wrong people and transgress upon the earth without right; for them is a painful punishment. But whoever is patient and forgives, indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination."

[Meaning] those who initiate it. [Then] "And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no protector after Him", i.e., no one who guides him or protects him from the punishment of Allah.

"And you will see the wrongdoers" — the disbelievers — "when they see the punishment, saying, 'Is there any way to return?'" — i.e., a return to the world.

"And you will see them exposed to it" — i.e., to the Fire — "humbled, from abasement they look with a furtive glance," meaning a glance that is weak, having been hidden out of abasement. This was said by Ibn Abbas. Mujahid, Qatada, al-Suddi and al-Qurazi said: they are stealthy glancers.

The scholars of language differed about the meaning of this verse. Yunus said: "min" here means "bi" (with), so the sense is "with a furtive glance," i.e., a weak glance from abasement and fear. Al-Akhfash said: "al-tarf" means the eye, so they look with a weak eye. It was also said: He only said "with a furtive glance" because they do not open their eyes fully but look with part of them. It was also said: the meaning is that they look at the Fire with their hearts, because they will be gathered blind, and looking with the heart is hidden.

And those who believe will say: "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in lasting punishment. And they will have no protectors to help them other than Allah. And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no path," i.e., no route to reach the truth in this world or Paradise in the hereafter, as the paths of good have been closed to him.

"Respond to your Lord" — with faith and obedience — "before there comes a Day that cannot be turned back from Allah. You will have no refuge" — a place of safety — "that Day, and you will have no denial" — no one to change your condition.

But if they turn away, We have not sent you as a guardian over them; your duty is only to convey. Indeed, when We cause man to taste mercy from Us, he rejoices in it; but if some evil befalls them because of what their hands have sent forth, then indeed man is ungrateful. To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows females upon whom He wills, so that he has no male child.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi related to us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Faraj related to us: Ahmad ibn al-Khalil al-Qawmi related to us: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us: Hakim ibn Hizam Abu Samir related to us, from Makhul, from Wathila ibn al-Asqa, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, among the blessings of a woman is that she is quick to bear a daughter before a son. That is because Allah the Exalted says: 'He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills.' Do you not see that He began with the females before the males?"

And He bestows males upon whom He wills, so that he has no female child. Or He pairs them, males and females, so that He causes him to have both males and females. The Arabs say: "I married" and "I married off," meaning the young to the old, i.e., I joined some of them with others.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Talha and Ubayd related to us, both saying: Ibn Mujahid related to us: al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn al-Abbas related to us: Sahl ibn Uthman related to us: Ubayd Allah related to us, from Isma'il ibn Sulayman, from Abu Umar, from Ibn al-Hanafiyya, concerning His words: "Or He pairs them, males and females." He said: twins.

"And He makes whom He wills barren, so that he neither bears children nor has children born to him."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us: al-Hasan ibn Alawiyya related to us: Isma'il ibn Isa related to us: Ishaq ibn Bishr related to us, concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted: "He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills, or pairs them, males and females, and makes whom He wills barren." He said: it was revealed concerning the prophets (peace be upon them), and then it became general. "He bestows females upon whom He wills": meaning Lot (peace be upon him), who had no male child, but only two daughters. "And bestows males upon whom He wills": meaning Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who had no female child. "Or pairs them, males and females": meaning the Prophet ﷺ, to whom were born sons and daughters. "And makes whom He wills barren": meaning Yahya and Isa (peace be upon them).

Indeed, He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful.

She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, your children are a gift [of Allah] to you: 'He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills.' [They and] their wealth belong to you when you are in need of them."

Ali ibn al-Hasan said: Yahya ibn Ma'in asked me about this hadith.

And those who answer their Lord, establish prayer, conduct their affairs by mutual consultation, and spend out of what We have provided them. It was said: these verses were revealed about Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, when people blamed him for spending all of his wealth, and when he was insulted and showed forbearance.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba related to us: Ishaq ibn Sadaqa related to us: Abd Allah ibn Hashim related to us: Sayf ibn Umar related to us, from Atiyya, from Ayyub, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Once Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, came into possession of wealth, and he gave all of it in charity for the cause of good. He specified it for Abu Bakr and extended it to those who followed him.

And those who, when wrong is inflicted upon them, defend themselves: they take revenge on their oppressors without transgressing.

Muqatil said: this refers to the one who has been wounded, who takes revenge on the one who wounded him and seeks retaliation against him. Ibrahim said: in this verse, they disliked being humiliated, and when they had the power, they pardoned.

"And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it." The recompense is named after the initial act, although it is not an evil, because the two resemble each other in form. Ibn Najih said: it means that the one who utters an ugly word is answered with its like; so if he says, "May Allah disgrace him," the response is, "May Allah disgrace him." Al-Suddi said: if he insults you with an insult, then insult him with its like, without transgressing.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn Hanash the reciter related to us: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl related to us: Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Abi Umar related to us. Sufyan ibn Uyayna said: I said to Sufyan al-Thawri: What is the meaning of His words, "And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it"? Is it that a man insults you and you insult him, or that he does something to you and you do the same to him? He had no answer for me, so I asked Hisham ibn Hujayr about this verse. He said: if a wounder wounds, you retaliate against him; it is not that he curses you and you curse him.

Sufyan said: Ibn Shubruma used to say: "Is there not in Makka someone like Hisham ibn Hujayr?" [He said this] regarding "But whoever pardons and reconciles..." [meaning] one who did not take revenge.

Ibn Abbas said: "whoever gives up retaliation and makes reconciliation." Muqatil said: pardon is among the righteous deeds, so its reward is upon Allah.

He said: a great multitude will stand up. He said: [Then] it will be said: "What is your reward with Allah?" They will say: "We are those who pardoned those who wronged us." That is His words, "But whoever pardons and reconciles, his reward is upon Allah." Then it will be said to them: "Enter Paradise by the permission of Allah."

Indeed, Allah does not love the wrongdoers. Ibn Abbas said: [They are] those who initiate the wrong, due to His words: "And whoever avenges himself after being wronged, those have no path [of blame] against them. The path is only against those who wrong people and transgress upon the earth without right; for them is a painful punishment. But whoever is patient and forgives, indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination."

[Meaning] those who initiate it. [Then] "And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no protector after Him", i.e., no one who guides him or protects him from the punishment of Allah.

"And you will see the wrongdoers" — the disbelievers — "when they see the punishment, saying, 'Is there any way to return?'" — i.e., a return to the world.

It was also said: the meaning is that they look at the Fire with their hearts, because they will be gathered blind, and looking with the heart is hidden.

Indeed, when We cause man to taste mercy from Us, he rejoices in it; but if some evil befalls them because of what their hands have sent forth, then indeed man is ungrateful. To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows females upon whom He wills, so that he has no male child.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi related to us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Faraj related to us: Ahmad ibn al-Khalil al-Qawmi related to us: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us: Hakim ibn Hizam Abu Samir related to us, from Makhul, from Wathila ibn al-Asqa, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, among the blessings of a woman is that she is quick to bear a daughter before a son. That is because Allah the Exalted says: 'He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills.' Do you not see that He began with the females before the males?"

And He bestows males upon whom He wills, so that he has no female child. Or He pairs them, males and females, so that He causes him to have both males and females. The Arabs say: "I married" and "I married off," meaning the young to the old, i.e., I joined some of them with others.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Talha and Ubayd related to us, both saying: Ibn Mujahid related to us: al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn al-Abbas related to us: Sahl ibn Uthman related to us: Ubayd Allah related to us, from Isma'il ibn Sulayman, from Abu Umar, from Ibn al-Hanafiyya, concerning His words: "Or He pairs them, males and females." He said: twins.

"And He makes whom He wills barren, so that he neither bears children nor has children born to him."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us: al-Hasan ibn Alawiyya related to us: Isma'il ibn Isa related to us: Ishaq ibn Bishr related to us, concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted: "He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills, or pairs them, males and females, and makes whom He wills barren." He said: it was revealed concerning the prophets (peace be upon them), and then it became general. "He bestows females upon whom He wills": meaning Lot (peace be upon him), who had no male child, but only two daughters. "And bestows males upon whom He wills": meaning Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who had no female child. "Or pairs them, males and females": meaning the Prophet ﷺ, to whom were born sons and daughters. "And makes whom He wills barren": meaning Yahya and Isa (peace be upon them).

Indeed, He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful.

Abu Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Mukhalidi informed us by dictation: Abu Nu'aym Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn Adi informed us: Ammar ibn Raja and Ali ibn Sahl ibn al-Mughira related to us, both saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq related to us: Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us: Ibn Wahb related to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id related to us: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq related to us: Abu Hamza al-Sukkari al-Marwazi related to us, from Ibrahim al-Sa'igh, from Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, from al-Aswad, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her.

She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, your children are a gift [of Allah] to you: 'He bestows females upon whom He wills and bestows males upon whom He wills.' [They and] their wealth belong to you when you are in need of them."

Ali ibn al-Hasan said: Yahya ibn Ma'in asked me about this hadith.

And those who answer their Lord, establish prayer, conduct their affairs by mutual consultation, and spend out of what We have provided them. It was said: these verses were revealed about Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, when people blamed him for spending all of his wealth, and when he was insulted and showed forbearance.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba related to us: Ishaq ibn Sadaqa related to us: Abd Allah ibn Hashim related to us: Sayf ibn Umar related to us, from Atiyya, from Ayyub, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Once Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, came into possession of wealth, and he gave all of it in charity for the cause of good. The Muslims blamed him and the disbelievers criticized him, so Allah the Exalted revealed: "So whatever you have been given is but the enjoyment of this worldly life..." up to His words: "and from what We have provided them they spend." He specified it for Abu Bakr and extended it to those who followed him.

And those who, when wrong is inflicted upon them, defend themselves: they take revenge on their oppressors without transgressing.

Muqatil said: this refers to the one who has been wounded, who takes revenge on the one who wounded him and seeks retaliation against him. Ibrahim said: in this verse, they disliked being humiliated, and when they had the power, they pardoned.

"And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it." The recompense is named after the initial act, although it is not an evil, because the two resemble each other in form. Ibn Najih said: it means that the one who utters an ugly word is answered with its like; so if he says, "May Allah disgrace him," the response is, "May Allah disgrace him." Al-Suddi said: if he insults you with an insult, then insult him with its like, without transgressing.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn Hanash the reciter related to us: Abu al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl related to us: Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Abi Umar related to us. Sufyan ibn Uyayna said: I said to Sufyan al-Thawri: What is the meaning of His words, "And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it"? Is it that a man insults you and you insult him, or that he does something to you and you do the same to him? He had no answer for me, so I asked Hisham ibn Hujayr about this verse. He said: if a wounder wounds, you retaliate against him; it is not that he curses you and you curse him.

Sufyan said: Ibn Shubruma used to say: "Is there not in Makka someone like Hisham ibn Hujayr?" [He said this] regarding "But whoever pardons and reconciles..." [meaning] one who did not take revenge.

Ibn Abbas said: "whoever gives up retaliation and makes reconciliation." Muqatil said: pardon is among the righteous deeds, so its reward is upon Allah.

Ibn Fanjawayh, the just, said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Bishr related to us; Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Mulas al-Dimashqi informed us; Abu Abd Allah Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Bishr al-Qurashi related to us; Zuhayr ibn Abbad al-Mada'ini related to us; Sufyan ibn Uyayna related to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out: whoever has a reward with Allah, let him stand up." He said: a great multitude will stand up. He said: [Then] it will be said: "What is your reward with Allah?" They will say: "We are those who pardoned those who wronged us." That is His words, "But whoever pardons and reconciles, his reward is upon Allah." Then it will be said to them: "Enter Paradise by the permission of Allah."

Indeed, Allah does not love the wrongdoers. Ibn Abbas said: [They are] those who initiate the wrong, due to His words: "And whoever avenges himself after being wronged, those have no path [of blame] against them. The path is only against those who wrong people and transgress upon the earth without right; for them is a painful punishment. But whoever is patient and forgives, indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination."

[Meaning] those who initiate it. [Then] "And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no protector after Him", i.e., no one who guides him or protects him from the punishment of Allah.

"And you will see the wrongdoers" — the disbelievers — "when they see the punishment, saying, 'Is there any way to return?'" — i.e., a return to the world.

"And you will see them exposed to it" — i.e., to the Fire — "humbled, from abasement they look with a furtive glance," meaning a glance that is weak, having been hidden out of abasement. This was said by Ibn Abbas. Mujahid, Qatada, al-Suddi and al-Qurazi said: they are stealthy glancers.

The scholars of language differed about the meaning of this verse. Yunus said: "min" here means "bi" (with), so the sense is "with a furtive glance," i.e., a weak glance from abasement and fear. Al-Akhfash said: "al-tarf" means the eye, so they look with a weak eye. It was also said: He only said "with a furtive glance" because they do not open their eyes fully but look with part of them. It was also said: the meaning is that they look at the Fire with their hearts, because they will be gathered blind, and looking with the heart is hidden.

And those who believe will say: "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, the wrongdoers are in lasting punishment. And they will have no protectors to help them other than Allah. And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no path," i.e., no route to reach the truth in this world or Paradise in the hereafter, as the paths of good have been closed to him.

"Respond to your Lord" — with faith and obedience — "before there comes a Day that cannot be turned back from Allah. You will have no refuge" — a place of safety — "that Day, and you will have no denial" — no one to change your condition.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 42, verses 51–53:

﴿And it is not for a human being that Allah should speak to him, except by revelation, or from behind a veil, or that He sends a messenger and he reveals by His permission what He wills.﴾ The reason for revelation: The Jews said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Will you not speak with Allah and look at Him, if you are a prophet, as He spoke with Moses and Moses looked at Him? For we will not believe in you until you do that." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Did Moses not look at Allah?" Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And it is not for a human being that Allah should speak to him.﴾

﴿Except by revelation﴾ (wahy): He reveals to him as He wills, either by inspiration (ilham) or in a dream. ﴿Or from behind a veil﴾: such that he hears His speech without seeing Him, as He spoke to Moses (peace be upon him). ﴿Or He sends a messenger﴾ to him from the angels, either Jibril or someone else, ﴿and he reveals by His permission what He wills.﴾ ﴿Indeed He is Most High, All-Wise.﴾

Shayba, Nafi' and Hisham recited (aw yursil) with a raised lam (yursilu) as a new sentence (ibtida'), and (fa-yuhiya) with a sukun on the ya'. The rest recited with a fathah on the lam and the ya', coordinating them (ʿatf) with the place (mahall) of wahy, because its meaning is: "It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except that He reveal, or send."

﴿Indeed He is Most High, All-Wise.﴾ ﴿And thus﴾ means: just as We revealed to all Our other messengers, ﴿We have revealed to you a spirit (ruh) from Our command.﴾ Al-Hasan said: mercy. Ibn 'Abbas: prophethood. Al-Suddi: revelation. Al-Kalbi: a book. Rabi': Jibril. Malik ibn Dinar: meaning the Qur'an; he used to say: "O people of the Qur'an, what has the Qur'an sown in your hearts? For the Qur'an is the spring of the hearts, just as rain is the spring of the earth."

﴿You did not know, before the revelation, what the Book was, nor faith (al-iman)﴾: meaning the laws (shara'i') and landmarks (ma'alim) of faith.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: it means the call to faith. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: it means the people of faith, those who believe and those who do not. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Jarir said: faith in this place means prayer.

Its evidence is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And Allah would never let your faith (iman) go to waste﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah: 143).

﴿But We made it a light﴾: the pronoun is singular though there are two things, faith and the Qur'an, because the verb (fi'l) in the multiplicity of its names is in the position of the verb. Do you not see that you say: "Your coming and your going pleases me," and then make it singular though they are two.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿But We made it﴾ means faith; al-Suddi said: it means the Qur'an.

﴿We guide thereby whom We will of Our servants. And indeed you guide﴾ to make right and call. ﴿To a straight path, the path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Unquestionably, to Allah all matters are returned.﴾

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Wazzan informed us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shadhan related to us, al-Husayn ibn Muhammad related to us, Salih ibn Muhammad related to us, who said: I heard Abu Ma'shar narrate, from Sahl ibn Abi al-Ja'da and others, who said: a mushaf was burned and nothing remained of it except His saying, Exalted and Majestic: ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah all matters are returned﴾; and a mushaf was drowned and every word in it was effaced except His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah all matters are returned.﴾
